    <h1>The train and Guardian</h1>
    <p class="lede">Running, editing and cancelling the daily train and the weekly Guardian rotation.</p>

<main class="doc guide">
<div class="wrap" markdown="1">

{% raw %}
Both rotations share one idea: everyone eligible gets a turn before anyone gets a second one. That stretch is a **cycle**; when everyone has had their turn, a new cycle starts. Running them needs **Run the train** or **Run Guardian rotation** (officers by default). On Premium, either can run by itself on a schedule: see [**DC Dark Legion setup**](/guides/dcdl-setup/). On Free, run them by hand.

## Who is eligible

Only active players who are not on leave, with **confirmed attendance** at the events that count. Out of the box (the **Standard** rules):

- **Train:** at least one Guardian, Gotham, Krypton Rush or Forge Breach event in the last 7 days.
- **Guardian:** a Guardian or Gotham event in the last 7 days, with Guardian attendees picked first. Players with the **Officer/R4** rank are left out.

Your server can change these (see [**DC Dark Legion setup**](/guides/dcdl-setup/), Who the rotations may pick). The pool reports always follow your server's rules. Recording attendance properly is what keeps both rotations fair.

## The train

**Conductor:** the strongest players (with Standard rules, the top 15 by power with at least two attendances in the last week) take turns; the top 10 of them are picked first.

**Carriages:** everyone else with at least one attendance, placed by their seat preference where possible (players set it in `/my-profile`). The Conductor tier (top 15 by power), and anyone who has been Conductor this cycle, never take a carriage seat; the strongest of them may fill one only if nobody else is left.

**Running it:** `/train-run` shows a preview, only to you. **Reroll** any seat to pick someone else, or **Reset assigned players** for a fresh pick. Nothing is saved until **Finish and post**, so closing a preview costs nobody their turn. It refuses a day that already has a train; `force` replaces it.

**After posting:** once the seats are set in the game, press **Assigned in game ✅** on the post. That also sends each rider who has claimed their character a DM with their seat (members choose this in `/my-profile`); nothing is sent before it, so a preview or a changed run never messages anyone. The train departs four hours later: from then on the run cannot be cancelled, because those players really rode. **Edit train** changes a posted run's seats.

**Cancelling:** **Cancel run** on the post (it asks to confirm), or `/train-cancel`. The players go back into the pool as if they had not been picked. Not possible after departure.

`/train-reset-epoch` starts a new cycle by hand, so everyone becomes eligible again.

## Guardian

Each week every city gets a Banker, an Architect and a Researcher, alongside its city guardian. The rotation fills the posts from eligible players who have not held one this cycle. With Standard rules, players with the **Officer/R4** rank on the roster are left out, since they run the rotation; the **Archon/R5** is included.

**Running it:** `/guardian-run`, or the weekly schedule (Premium). It refuses a day that already has a run; `force` replaces that day's run entirely.

**On the post:** each city has a button to mark it **assigned in-game**, so other officers can see which cities are done. Pressing it also sends that city's players who have claimed their character a DM with their post.

**Edit rotation** opens an editor on that week: reroll a post (in a rotating city, someone from the city's group first), or **Reset assigned people** for fresh picks across the static cities. **Finish and post** saves it.

**Rotating cities:** a city in rotation mode is covered by its own group, who take turns at all four posts, guardian included. Set this up under **🏙️ Guardian cities** on the **DC Dark Legion** tab of `/guild-settings show` (see [**DC Dark Legion setup**](/guides/dcdl-setup/)). Reset leaves those cities alone.

## The reports

**📊 Reports** on the officer panel has buttons for the train and Guardian pools: who is waiting for a turn, who has not had one this cycle, and when each player last had one. These need **See rotation reports** (seniors and officers by default).
